local_feature_memberships.rationale: Distinct scoped-state precedence and alias-migration workflow with its own state authority and concurrency semantics.
Distinct governance boundary for retired bridge ownership and source-lineage non-ownership.
Distinct Free-Models Auto Apply lifecycle with last-known-good, concurrency, and crash-recovery semantics.
Distinct user-visible reconnect promise with a bounded retry state machine and outcome contract.
Distinct downloadable-artifact trust lifecycle for signing, provenance, and SBOM evidence.
Distinct configuration-schema migration workflow and fixture semantics.
Distinct generated-document link validation concern with cross-renderer acceptance and validation failure modes.
Distinct install-and-update flow provenance lifecycle and user-visible update failure state.
Distinct platform compatibility matrix and launch-failure recovery concern.
Distinct governance gates for release migration, backup, restore, and rollback.
Distinct receipt data contract consumed by signing, update, migration, and related release workflows.
Distinct runtime command that restores a selected safe point and retries a run under transactional execution semantics.
Distinct restore-point artifact envelope and restore lifecycle, separate from commands that consume it.
Distinct unsaved-file snapshot identity, retention, and cleanup lifecycle.
Distinct storage-wrapper and command-vocabulary migration lifecycle.
Distinct bulk-action partial-success rollback and compensation state machine.
Distinct durable-storage recovery coordination across fallback, quarantine, shutdown, backup, restore, and destructive authority.

relationships.rationale: Config-schema migration is a migration workflow whose lifecycle is constrained by release migration and rollback gates, but it has different authority and executable semantics.
Install and update flows produce provenance receipts, while receipt field semantics and lifecycle rules are owned by the separate release receipt contract.
Signing, provenance, and SBOM evidence uses release receipt contracts without becoming the same product feature as the receipt data model.
The restore-and-retry command consumes an identified safe-point artifact, but command authority, retry behavior, and atomicity remain distinct from artifact schema and restore integrity.
Storage migration can encounter backup, rollback, fallback, and destructive recovery behavior, while command-vocabulary migration and durable-store recovery retain different lifecycles and consumers.
Durable backup and restore operations can produce or consume restore-point artifacts, but the artifact envelope and broad storage recovery coordinator have different authorities and failure surfaces.
